newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NORTHERN IRELAND TOLD TO PREPARE FOR ALBANIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NORTHERN IRELAND TOLD TO PREPARE FOR ALBANIA.

text.p: Northern Ireland have been instructed by FIFA to plan ahead as scheduled for the World Cup qualifier with Albania in Belfast on December 14.

Football Association officials contacted world soccer's governing body immediately after hearing that the Albanians had been suspended from the international arena following an internal political dispute.
A ruling on the immediate future of the Albanians is expected on Tuesday but Irish spokesman John Quinn said today: "FIFA have advised us to continue with our plans for the game as usual.
"We are doing just that. We assume that the game will go ahead as scheduled and the tickets will go out today and the players have been told that things will be continuing as normal.
"Of course, nothing is ever certain in football, but we have been told to continue full steam ahead and that's what we're doing. We are confident that the game will take place as arranged."
FIFA imposed the sanction after hearing that Albanian Football Association general secretary Eduard Dervishi had been suspended and the executive committee dissolved by the country's sports ministry.
Albanian sports secretary Marjeta Pronjari censured Dervishi for consistently postponing new executive committee elections, a move which apparently breaks the country's civil law.
But FIFA invoked the ban by insisting they did not recognise the suspensions and still considered Dervishi and the dissolved executive as their only official contacts in the country.

Albanian prime minister Aleksander Meksi immediately made a bid to solve the row by appealing to the soccer federation and the state sports secretariat to put aside their differences. He also recommended that new executive committee elections be held in February.
A statement from his office read: "The prime minister will propose to the council of ministers an annulment of decisions relating to the suspensions of various soccer federation officials.
"The government pledges to take the necessary steps to overcome present difficulties so that Albanian soccer can remain on the international map."
FIFA spokesman Keith Cooper said: "There is no news from our side yet, but the conciliatory signs that we've seen and heard over the weekend look encouraging."
